event: Pakistan Floods 2022 — Khairpur District, Sindh reference timeline
selection_reason: Khairpur District was selected as the study area because credible 2022 UNOSAT products report satellite-detected floodwater and inundated agricultural areas in and around Khairpur, providing a defensible historical case for Sentinel-based flood and crop-recovery analysis.

observations.summary: UNOSAT's Sindh flood assessment included Khairpur District in its district-level table of satellite-detected water extent.
UNOSAT's 9 September flood-evolution assessment showed inundated agricultural areas surrounding Khairpur city in Khairpur District.
UNOSAT continued to report extensive flooding across Sindh during mid-September; this period provides regional context but must not be treated as a single-date Khairpur ground-truth map.

A later UNOSAT weekly assessment reported approximately 400 km² of receding floodwaters in Khairpur District, supporting a historical recession/recovery narrative rather than exact inundation-duration claims.

limitations: UNOSAT products are preliminary satellite analyses and are not equivalent to field-validated ground truth.
Some reference products are cumulative or multi-day assessments and must not be directly compared with a single Sentinel acquisition without temporal matching.
The offline replay stores verified source metadata and published context, not fabricated flood polygons.
Khairpur city and Khairpur District are distinct spatial concepts; the project uses Khairpur District as the primary study area and Khairpur Mir's as the city reference point.
